subject: Preparing a room for installation
hook: Do I have to empty the whole room before you fit?
fb:
One of the questions we get asked most: do I need to empty the whole room before you fit?

Usually not. The wall where the furniture is going needs to be completely clear, and there needs to be a decent working area in front of it for the team to lay out panels and tools. The rest of the room can often stay as it is, as long as it's covered and out of the way.

Anything fragile or precious is best moved out. We'll tell you exactly what's needed for your room when we come to measure, so there's no guesswork on the day.

Got another question about installation? Ask away, or book a free consultation here:

gbp:
Do I need to empty the whole room before my fitted furniture is installed?

Not always. The wall where the furniture will go must be completely clear, including shelves, picture hooks, curtain poles and wall-mounted TVs, and there needs to be enough open floor in front of it for our team to lay out panels and work safely. Other furniture in the room can usually stay if it's covered and moved back.

We'd always suggest moving fragile or valuable items out of the room altogether. It's also worth making sure plastering, decorating near the wall and any electrical work are finished before the day.

Every room is different, so we confirm exactly what's needed at the measuring visit. Our own team makes the furniture in our Hanley workshop and fits it, so the advice you get comes from the people doing the job.

Book a free, no-obligation design consultation to talk your room through.
